checklist_items.22.1: covered: every entry the shell actually renders in the sider is enumerated at runtime (19 of them, read from .app-sider .app-nav rather than from a route table) and each is entered by deep link in both en and zh. For each entry the case asserts the address it settles on, that exactly one menu entry is selected, that the selected entry is that same entry, and that a non-empty page title is rendered; then it calls page.reload() and re-asserts the same address, the same selected entry and the same title, so the position is proven to survive a refresh rather than only on entry. A child route is accepted only where the product itself redirects: /analytics settles on /analytics/usage (AnalyticsPage.tsx:98) and the address is read after the page renders, so the pre-redirect address is never mistaken for the landing one. The deployments surface is covered in its own right: /deployments keeps selected=Deployments with title Deployments, and /deployments?deployment=<id> rebuilds the same title, the same highlight and the same drawer title after a reload.
checklist_items.22.2: covered for the deployments surface, which owns a URL parameter of its own: the list keeps its open detail in the address (?deployment=<id>, DeploymentsPage.tsx:130), so the address, the highlighted menu entry and the page title are three independent witnesses that must agree. Two entries are visited by clicking the menu, then page.go_back() and page.go_forward() each assert all three together - address, selected entry and title - so a restored address with a stale highlight or title fails. The ?deployment=<id> deep link opens the drawer with the matching title and leaves the highlight unchanged; page.reload() keeps the parameter, the drawer and the same drawer title; Escape clears the parameter while the address, the highlight and the title still agree. Entries are addressed by their menu key rather than their label, because the label is translated and this case runs in both languages.
checklist_items.22.3: covered for the single role this build can create, with the administrator-only branch recorded and deliberately not claimed. User.Role has exactly one write point and it hardcodes admin (internal/server/store/auth.go:31), so no product path creates a second role and an admin-versus-user comparison cannot be built from two real identities. What is asserted: the session's own role read from /api/v1/auth/me is admin; all 19 sider entries are rendered for it; and a direct call to GET /api/v1/deployments made outside the page's own requests, carrying only the session cookie, answers 200 with an items/total list. The 403 ErrorAdministratorRequired branch at internal/server/api/auth.go:240 does exist and is recorded as existing, but reaching it needs signed claims carrying a non-admin role, which requires the master key; a forged token would be neither a real user path nor honest evidence, so it is not claimed. GPUWorks does not use the Router organization/IAM model: there is no organization scope, role-assignment UI or per-resource IAM policy to enumerate.
checklist_items.22.4: covered by making a real session expire under real polling. The cookie cannot witness this: the product writes it with the session's absolute deadline on login and on renewal alike (internal/server/api/auth.go:76 and :219 both pass AbsoluteExpiresAt), so its expiry never reflects idle renewal - an earlier attempt compared that value and its own positive control rejected it as sub-second float jitter. Instead a second isolated server runs the product's own session_idle_timeout key at 3s; the session performs real GET polls of /api/v1/auth/me for 6.8s, twice the deadline. The first 7 polls answer 200 and the last 9 answer 401, with the first 401 at 3.17s, so the session expired on schedule while being polled: a passive poll is not human activity and cannot renew it. This matches the product rule that renewal sits in a branch that skips GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (api/auth.go:213-219). The second server is stopped in a finally block.
checklist_items.22.5: covered for the navigation, the first screen, the table's live text and the not-found surface, in en and in zh in the same contract (two full runs). Expectations are read from the shipped locale files rather than copied, so they are the product's own wording. In each language the case asserts that the locale's own navigation label for deployments is rendered and that the other language's label is not; that the page title equals the locale's deployments page title and is not the other language's; and that every table column header is translated text, with an explicit rejection of any header that looks like an internal field name (snake_case, or camelCase starting lowercase). The not-found page's own title and description are asserted in the same locale.
checklist_items.22.6: covered by real keyboard operation and computed style, on the deployments list while the deployment still exists (its disabled controls derive from the running state, DeploymentsPage.tsx:243-244, so a deleted deployment would leave nothing to read). focus-visible is reached the way a keyboard user reaches it: body is clicked to reset focus and Tab is pressed 14 times, and for each landed element getComputedStyle is read; 4 of them painted a real outline and the measured widths were 2px and 3px, so the ring is a painted outline of measurable width rather than a zero-width placeholder or a focus() call that would not prove keyboard reachability. Colour and disabled state come from the browser too: the 4 controls rendered as disabled were each confirmed genuinely disabled by attribute or aria, and the selected entry's computed colour (rgb(0, 91, 212)) was read again after a reload and found unchanged, which is a theme value rather than a one-off literal.
checklist_items.22.7: covered for the SPA fallback and the error surface, which is where this item bites: an address that has no route is answered directly with 200 and content-type text/html, so the status alone cannot distinguish a real page from one that has no route. The case records that 200, then loads the address in the browser and asserts that the app rendered its own not-found title, its own description, and the exact address it was given - so a wrong or dead deep link cannot hide behind the fallback. It also asserts that no sider entry is highlighted, since a highlight would claim the page exists, and that the not-found page's own recovery action reaches a real deployments page with a rendered title. The link targets are taken from the locale files, so the same assertions hold in en and zh.
checklist_items.10.1: covered for the populated and the filtered-empty state. The list was read populated with twelve real rows and the row count was compared against the total the product itself reports in its own header (both twelve, and the server's total equals the items it returned); the empty state was then reached through the product's own search box with a term that matches nothing, which rendered no rows and the product's filtered-empty wording ('No deployments match the search or state' in en, '没有符合搜索或状态筛选的部署' in zh) rather than the never-created text, so the two meanings of empty stay distinguishable to a user. A failed list request and the loading state are not constructed by this case and are not claimed here.
checklist_items.10.2: covered for a complete term, a fragment, an absent term, a wildcard character and a cleared box, each with the request captured. The list searches on the server (DeploymentsPage.tsx:99 puts q into the request), so a client-side filter over already-fetched rows would look identical on screen; the captured request is therefore compared with the rows returned. A complete deployment name returned exactly that one row with q equal to the term; a six-character fragment returned the matching rows with that fragment as q; a term matching nothing returned no rows; a bare '%' returned no rows at all (0 of 12), so the term was treated as a literal character rather than a wildcard reaching the query unescaped; and clearing the box restored the original twelve rows.
checklist_items.10.4: covered for the created-at column, which sorts on the server. Two clicks on the header sent different sort parameters to the server ('created_at' then '-created_at'), the rendered row order changed between the two clicks, and both orders contained the same set of rows, so the reversal is a real re-sort rather than a re-render. The request was captured because reading the rendered order alone cannot distinguish a server sort from a stale first page.
checklist_items.10.5: covered for all four page sizes the table offers. PAGE_SIZE_OPTIONS is [10, 20, 50, 100] (ui/src/components/resourceTable/columnPrefs.ts:27) and the list is server-paged, so each choice was checked in both the request and the result: selecting 10, 20, 50 and 100 in turn sent page_size=10/20/50/100 respectively, and with twelve rows available size 10 rendered ten rows while 20, 50 and 100 each rendered all twelve. The differing counts are what proves the choice reached the server instead of falling back to a default; the total was read from the server rather than assumed, because the list also holds the deployment this case owns. Antd formats the option label per locale ('20 / page' in en, '20 条/页' in zh), and both locales were run.
checklist_items.10.6: covered with all four parts. At page size 10 the twelve rows made two pages. Next and previous were both operated: previous was asserted disabled on the first page and next disabled on the last, and the active page marker moved 1 to 2 and back. Every row was collected page by page by the deployment name it renders and compared as a set against the unpaged list the server reports: twelve names collected, twelve distinct, no repeats, and no row absent from or extra to the server's list - a count comparison alone would not have shown this, since two pages could still repeat one row and omit another. Going back to the first page restored the same names in the same order. Both page collections are recorded in the report for audit.
checklist_items.10.7: covered for deleting the last batch row on the last page. With twelve rows at page size 10 the last page held two rows; the final one of them was deleted, restricted to a row this section created because the page can also hold the deployment this case owns. The server's total fell from 12 to 11 and the deleted row appeared in neither the re-rendered page nor the server's list, and the view did not leave the user on a page with no rows while eleven rows still existed. The page size, the page count and the row set after the deletion are recorded in the report.
checklist_items.10.3: covered for all ten filters the state column offers, and for a combination that is populated on both sides and empty where they meet. The options are the product's own: DeploymentsPage.tsx:213 builds them from DEPLOYMENT_LIST_STATES and :97 passes them on as the state parameter, which api.ts:916 joins with commas. Each of the ten was ticked in the column's own filter popup and applied, and the request it caused was captured: every one carried its own state value, and the rows rendered equalled the total the server reports for that same state (the running state 1 of 1, the queued state 10 of 10, the other eight 0 of 0). The two populated states are asserted on their row sets; the eight that return an empty set were still executed and their parameters checked, and are recorded as measured rather than as failing states, because this fixture holds deployments in two of the ten states only. The server really validates the value (finished, bogus and Running all answer 400 LIST_FILTER_INVALID), so the empty results are genuinely empty and not an ignored parameter. The combination requirement is met with a state filter and a search term that each return rows alone - the term resolves to one row still waiting for a device, and state=running returns its own row - while the two together return none, and both sides use the same term so the empty intersection comes from the state rather than from two unrelated conditions. The same run was made in both locales.
checklist_items.10.9: covered for the action that opens in place, with the other two the item names recorded as the shape this product actually gives them. Each row's name cell is a link button (DeploymentsPage.tsx:159 renders the name inside a Button that opens the detail), so three rows were each reached by their own unique business text - row00, row01 and row02, distinct names - and each opened a drawer titled with that same name and mentioning it in its body, which shows the click opened that row's detail rather than whichever row came first. Every drawer was asserted fully inside the viewport at its own bounding box (x 720..1440 and y 0..900 of a 1440x900 viewport) and the window's scrollY was unchanged between opening and closing, so the fit is not the automatic scrolling the item warns about; the address named each row's own id while open, and closing removed the drawer entirely. The other two actions do not open in place in this product and are stated as they are rather than folded into the measured one: edit is a full-page navigation to /deploy?edit=<id> (DeploymentsPage.tsx:255), because editing a deployment is applied to a whole wizard draft; and diagnose is not a row action at all - the only diagnose entry is task=instance.diagnose inside ui/src/pages/InstancePanel.tsx:260, which ui/src/pages/DeploymentInstances.tsx:32 mounts on its own page, and searching ui/src/pages/DeploymentsPage.tsx and ui/src/pages/deploy/ for diagnose returns nothing.
checklist_items.10.10: covered, with the refresh kinds separated because this product does not treat them as one behaviour. The item names a manual refresh and a background update together; measured, they differ, and all three cases are asserted: a background poll keeps the filter (with a state filter applied, the 8s poll at DeploymentsPage.tsx:101 re-requested the list carrying that same state value, evidenced by the captured request rather than by the row count alone, and the filtered rows were unchanged), opening and closing a row's detail keeps the filter (that path changes only the address, :130 and :131, so the filter survived with the same rows), and a manual reload drops it and shows the whole list - which is this product's contract rather than a failure, because the search and the chosen states are plain component state (:95, :96) and are written to neither the address nor localStorage. A row deleted with no filter applied was then gone from three independent readings: it answered 404 on the server, it was absent from the rendered list across another poll, and it was absent from the server's own unfiltered list, so its absence cannot be explained by a filter. Unsaved drafts do not apply to this surface: a draft is held by the /deploy wizard, and this page polls list data only, so there is no draft here for a poll to overwrite.

10.8 needs real owned populations of 10, 30 and 100 deployments; 100 deployments means 100 real containers per run, which is not a cost this suite can pay. Left open rather than declared not applicable, because the product can hold that many - the limit is the test's economy, not the surface.

10.3 (every real filter executed independently and a two-condition combination whose intersection is empty) is not declared: the state column's filters were observed to exist (DeploymentsPage.tsx:213-214) but this case does not select each of the ten states in turn, so the item stays open rather than being claimed from the presence of the control.
10.11 (grouping and subtotals) does not apply to this surface: the deployments list renders a flat ResourceTable with no grouped or summary projection (ui/src/pages/DeploymentsPage.tsx:263-291).
